description: Southern Thai prayer hall under a large ribbed dome with smaller corner domes and a single slender minaret alongside.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Rectangular prayer hall under one large ribbed onion dome on a drum, four smaller matching domes at the roof corners, a single slender tapering minaret alongside topped with a small domed balcony and a crescent finial, arched arcade of pointed horseshoe arches along the entrance front, low boundary wall with an arched gateway Materials: White and pale green painted render with damp staining low on the walls, green glazed dome ribs, gold crescent finials, weathered whitewash on the boundary wall, dark mildew streaks under the eaves.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92 -- not a pass self-score. Second build: the declared 18 m corrected to the proxy's 12, and the hall, loggia, drum, corner domes and engaged minaret all re-authored off the proxy depth maps and the plate crops at 3x. Band table 0.026 / 0.032 of height. 17,088/32,000 triangles, 13/24 draw calls, 7/16 materials, 13/32 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: Great dome r 2.40 on a r 2.25 drum with twelve pointed windows, crown at 9.50, crescent to 10.85; a square tapering minaret (1.32 -> 1.04 m) engaged with the left wall at x -5.05 z -2.90, corbelled octagonal balcony at 9.10, eight-arch lantern to 10.50, ribbed dome and crescent to 12.00. Band table against the Meshy proxy: bands 5-9 (the dome and minaret zone) agree within 0.033 on width; the first build's bands 5-8 were off by 0.16-0.36.
featureReviews.notes: The first build stood the minaret CLEAR of the hall at x -5.75 because the registry notes said so; the proxy's TOP map puts its shaft inside the hall's left edge (cols 15-24, rows -0.18..-0.24 H) and the plate's shaft rises from behind the roof with no base visible, which is an engaged tower. Residual: the ornament and lantern span 0.04-0.07 of height more in z than the proxy's at bands 7-8.

featureReviews.evidence: Three 1.55 m Moorish doorways (shoulder 2.65, apex 3.85, from proxy rows 650 / 570) cut through a 0.6 m screen wall onto an open loggia 1.8 m deep, its inner wall the pale green the plate paints it (#B8C1AA lit, PBR confidence 0.860); two narrower blind niches at +-4.15 with a white surround and a raised inner arch panel on the same green field. The front turntable frame shows the inner wall through every opening at luma well above the backdrop.
featureReviews.notes: The first build's arcade was five dark panels PROUD of a solid block, because 'the hall is a solid mass'. The plate's arcade crop at 3x shows the piers casting shadows onto a wall two metres behind them, and the proxy's +Z depth map reads the openings 1.6-2.1 m behind the face. Residual: the plate's loggia floor and inner wall carry their own shading the harness's flatter key does not reproduce.

featureReviews.evidence: Four ribbed corner domes r 1.00 on ringed drums at (+-4.18, -4.40 / +2.50) -- the proxy's 801 px and side-map 225 / 675 px -- with tops at 7.16 against the proxy's 7.18; gilt spikes; the cap-ball-bulb-spike-crescent stack over the great dome and, at 0.4 scale, over the minaret. Corner drums spring from the deck at 5.06, 0.62 m below the great dome's podium lip.
featureReviews.notes: The corner domes now stand at the roof CORNERS on drums the deck can be seen under, where the first build's sat at +-3.40 on a 9.2 m hall. Residual: the plate's corner drums carry a small moulded base ring this build folds into the drum's top ring.

featureReviews.evidence: Turntable gate run with --allow-holes and the measurement that justifies it: the enclosed-background components at 090 and 270 are the COURTYARD (14,302 px, 125 x 153 bbox, mean thickness 93 px), and at 000 the courtyard strips either side of the hall (3,768 px, 19 px thick). Nothing enclosed is a surface of the model.
featureReviews.notes: A walled compound has real open ground between its enclosure wall and its hall, and from any three-quarter view the silhouette encloses that background on all four sides. The flag is set on that finding rather than to get past an unexplained failure, as in the first build; the loggia openings themselves land on the lit inner wall and are not flagged.

featureReviews.evidence: Seven materials at PBR confidence 0.751-0.860, every albedo measured off the plate; three seeded canvas tiles carry the rain-wash from the TOP of every part down. Matched windows: dome mean luma 140.6 against the plate's 133.9; front field 169 against the plate's lit 199 and side wall 149 against its shaded 121 (the harness has a flatter key than the plate and the two windows straddle it); deck 154 against 107, the plate's window including its own shadowed stains.
featureReviews.notes: The first build carried the streak DIRECTION as a vertex gradient and no streaks. The tile's v is keyed to each part's top, which needed CanvasTexture.flipY = false -- with the default flip the whole streak band landed a tile-height below every wall and only the mottle showed, as leopard spots. Residual: the plate's streaks cluster; the tile's are more even.

name: Mosque
notes: Most numerous in the southern provinces, and the recognisable pairing is one large ribbed dome plus a single slender minaret standing clear of the hall -- that two-part silhouette is what reads at distance and neither element works alone. Declared at 18 m tall, well above the building-part category's 8 m prior, because the minaret rather than the hall sets the height. Green and white are the usual colours and the prompt names both so the plate does not come back in the gold and orange of a Buddhist temple. No destruction groups: it is static landmark geometry. Height corrected 18 -> 12 m on 2026-09-01 from the Meshy proxy read with scratch/_mon/vox.mjs and front.mjs: the compound spans 1.77 x 1.90 proxy units in plan against 1.447 tall, so at the declared 14 x 16 footprint the minaret tip stands 11.6-12.3 m up (mean 12.0). The hall parapet is 0.455 of that (5.46 m), the dome crown 0.79 (9.5 m), and the minaret reaches 2.2 times the hall -- the plate agrees: its minaret is about twice the hall's height, not 2.5 times a 7.2 m hall. Nothing about the 14 x 16 footprint changed.
